mainTopic: When a found גט is returned: busy places, known matching names, witnesses, and exact סימנים
overview: A גט was found in רב הונא's court, and the worry was that it might belong to a different couple with the same names. רבה found a משנה saying court documents are returned. The גמרא learns from this that even in a busy place, we only hold back the גט if we know there are two people with the same names. There are two versions of רבה's real case in the flax area of פומבדיתא. רבי זירא resolves a clash between a משנה and a ברייתא by saying it depends on whether caravans of travelers are common. The גמרא asks whether he agrees with רבה, and how each one reads the court-documents משנה. Then רבי ירמיה says the גט is returned when the witnesses signed only one such גט. רב אשי says it is returned when the owner gives a very exact mark, because he is unsure whether סימנים work by Torah law. The amud ends as a story about רבה בר בר חנה begins.

steps.title: רב הונא worries about two towns named שוירי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says we must worry that there are two towns named שוירי, so the found גט may belong to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that there may be two places called שוירי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his first reaction to a גט found in his court: maybe there is another town with the same name, so we cannot be sure whose גט this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a different couple with the same names, living in another town called שוירי, could be the real owners. If so, giving the גט to the wrong woman could be a serious mistake. This sets up the question that רבה will be asked to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned / we worry about
The name of a town written in the found גט

phrases.english: We are concerned about two places called Sheviri,
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא speaking, about a גט found in his court that named the town שוירי.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָיְישִׁינַן לִשְׁנֵי שְׁוִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the גט found in רב הונא's court, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a concern that a second town with the same name exists, so the גט might not be returned.

steps.title: רב חסדא sends רבה to investigate
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה to research the question, because רב הונא will ask him about it in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבה: Go and look into this, because tonight רב הונא will ask you about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: the question is handed to רבה to research. The גמרא is preparing for רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given yet. The step turns רב הונא's worry into an open question that needs a source. It tells us the answer will come from רבה.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said to Rabba:
Go out and examine it,
for in the evening Rav Huna will ask you about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה פּוֹק עַיֵּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב הונא's worry and turns it into a question for רבה to research.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should a גט found in בית דין be returned, or do we worry it belongs to another couple?

steps.title: רבה finds a משנה: court documents are returned
steps.stepSummary: רבה researches and finds a משנה saying any document that went through בית דין should be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, looked carefully, and found the answer, as we learned in a משנה: any document of בית דין should be returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question with a משנה: documents of בית דין are returned to their owner. Since the גט was found in court, it should be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats papers connected to בית דין as safe to return. רבה applies this to the גט found in רב הונא's court. So the worry about a second שוירי does not stop us from returning it.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: He went out, examined carefully, and found.
As we learned: any court document
phrases.notes: This משנה appears a little later in this פרק, on דף כ.

phrases.english: he should return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק דַּק וְאַשְׁכַּח דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רב חסדא gave רבה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט found in בית דין counts as a court document and should be returned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer becomes the basis for the general rule the גמרא draws in the next step.

steps.title: Proof: worry only if two people with the same names are known
steps.stepSummary: Since רב הונא's court is busy like a place full of travelers, and רבה still said to return the גט, we only worry if we know of two people with the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, רב הונא's court is like a place where caravans are common, and רבה still ruled that the גט should be returned. So: if it is known that there are two people named יוסף בן שמעון, yes, we worry. If not, we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבה's ruling as a proof for the earlier question about busy places. Even where travelers are common, we only worry if two people with the same names are actually known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court draws people from many places, just like a town full of passing caravans. If רבה returned the גט even there, then busy traffic alone is not a reason to worry. The worry starts only when it is known that two people share the same names.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where caravans (travelers) are common

steps.whatToRemember: Even in a busy place full of travelers, we return a found גט unless we actually know there are two people with the same names.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה's ruling is not saying travelers don't matter at all. It says the deciding factor is whether two people with the same names are known to exist.

phrases.english: And the court of Rav Huna,
is like a place where caravans are common,
phrases.notes: People from many towns come to a court, so it is as busy as a place full of travelers.

phrases.english: and Rabba resolved that he should return it,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אִי הוּחְזְקוּ שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן – אִין,
phrases.english: evidently, if it is established that there are two Yosef ben Shimons, yes,
phrases.notes: יוסף בן שמעון is just a sample name, like 'John Smith'. 'Yes' means yes, we worry and don't return it.

phrases.english: if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּי דִינָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from רבה's answer.
steps.raayaObject: Even in a place where caravans are common, we only worry about another couple if two people with the same names are known.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה ruled to return the גט found in רב הונא's busy court.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for found גיטין in busy places.

steps.title: רבה rules in practice on a גט found in the פומבדיתא flax house
steps.stepSummary: רבה actually ruled, following his own view, about a גט found in the flax house of פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה made a practical ruling about a גט that was found in the flax house of פומבדיתא, following his own teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבה used his rule in a real case: a גט found in the flax house in פומבדיתא was returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows רבה's rule was not just theory but was applied in practice. 'כשמעתיה' means he ruled the same way he taught in רב הונא's case. The next step will clarify the details of this case.

phrases.english: Rabba performed an action regarding a certain bill of divorce
that was found in the flax house of Pumbedita, in accordance with his teaching.
phrases.notes: So he ordered that the גט be returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבַד רַבָּה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבה applying the rule from the previous step in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט found in the flax house of פומבדיתא was returned, following רבה's view.

steps.title: Another version: the flax market, despite many travelers
steps.stepSummary: Some say the case was in the flax market, and רבה returned the גט only because two people with the same names were not known, even though travelers were common.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: it was where they sell flax, and it was specifically because it was not established that there were two people with the same names, even though caravans are common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the details of רבה's case. It stresses that the place was busy with travelers, and he still returned the גט because no second couple was known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version makes the case match the rule from step 4 exactly. The busy flax market is like a place where caravans are common. רבה returned the גט only because it was not known that two people shared the same names.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's practical ruling: even in a busy market full of travelers, return the גט as long as no second person with the same names is known.

phrases.english: There are those who say: it was where they sell flax,
and specifically when it was not established,
phrases.notes: Meaning it was not known that two people with the same names lived there.

phrases.english: even though caravans are common.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי הֵיכָא דִּמְזַבְּנִי כִּיתָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the details of רבה's practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a flax market where travelers are common, the גט was returned because two people with the same names were not known.

steps.title: Second version of where רבה's case happened: the flax-soaking place
steps.stepSummary: According to the second version, רבה's case was in the place where flax is soaked. He returned the גט even though two people with the same names were known, because caravans do not come there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the case was in the place where they soak flax. רבה returned the גט even though it was known that there were two people with the same names, because caravans are not common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of where רבה's case happened and why he returned the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the deciding factor is whether caravans pass through, not whether two people share the same names. Since caravans are rare in the flax-soaking area, the גט almost certainly belongs to the local couple. That holds even though two couples with the same names were known.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: a second version of the story
It was established (here: two people with the same names were known)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the versions. The first version (step 6) is the flax market, where caravans are common and there were no known two people with the same names. This version is the flax-soaking place, where same names were known but caravans are rare. In both versions, רבה returned the גט.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
it was where they soak flax,
and even though they were established,
phrases.notes: Established meaning it was known that two couples had the same names.

phrases.english: since caravans are not common.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the case in step 6, with the facts reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where caravans are rare, a found גט is returned even if two people with the same names are known.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes the משנה: a lost גט is valid only if found right away
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא sets up a contradiction he will resolve. He starts with a משנה: a messenger who lost a גט may use it only if he found it right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא raised a contradiction between a משנה and a ברייתא and resolved it. We learned: if someone was bringing a גט and lost it, and he found it right away, it is valid. If not, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבי זירא first quotes a משנה, and he will soon contrast it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a גט found after some time is invalid. We worry it may be a different גט that belongs to another couple with the same names. This is the first side of the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises a contradiction (sets two sources against each other)
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised a contradiction between the mishnah and a baraita
and he resolved it.
We learned: one who is bringing a get
and it got lost from him,
if he found it right away, it is valid;
and if not, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא רָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין אַבָּרַיְיתָא וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new discussion that will use the same caravans idea from steps 6–7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost גט found right away is valid; if it is found later, it is invalid.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to return a found גט even after a long time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a גט found in the market is returned to the wife if the husband admits to it. That seems to apply even after a long time, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He contrasted it with a ברייתא: if someone found a woman's גט in the market and the husband admits to it, he should return it to the wife. If the husband does not admit, he should not return it to either of them. In any case, the ברייתא teaches that when the husband admits, it goes back to the wife, even after a long time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. The ברייתא returns a found גט without any time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say the גט must be found right away. So it seems to allow returning it even after a long time. The משנה, though, says a גט found later is invalid, and the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And he contrasted it (brought a source that seems to contradict)
Admits (the husband agrees he wrote and gave the גט)
In any event, it teaches: zooms in on the key words

phrases.english: And he contrasted it:
if one found a woman's get in the marketplace,
when the husband admits,
he should return it to the wife.
If the husband does not admit,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should return it neither to this one nor to that one.
phrases.notes: Neither to the husband nor to the wife.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
when the husband admits, he should return it to the wife,
and even after a long time!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposite side of the contradiction to the משנה in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a lost גט found later is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא returns a found גט with no time limit, so finding it later seems to be fine.

steps.title: Resolution: it depends on whether caravans are common
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the משנה is talking about a place where caravans are common. The ברייתא is talking about a place where caravans are rare.
steps.simpleTranslation: He resolved it: here, in the משנה, it is a place where caravans are common. There, in the ברייתא, it is a place where caravans are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where many travelers pass through, a גט found later might belong to a stranger with the same names, so the משנה invalidates it. Where travelers are rare, the found גט surely belongs to the local couple, so the ברייתא returns it even after a long time. This uses the same caravans idea as רבה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... and there: each source refers to a different case

steps.whatToRemember: A found גט is returned or used based on how likely it is to belong to someone else. Where caravans are common, we worry about strangers with the same names. Where caravans are rare, we don't.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי זירא, like רבה in the second version, treats passing caravans as the main thing to check when deciding about a lost גט.

phrases.english: And he resolved it:
here, it is in a place where caravans are common,
phrases.notes: Here means the משנה, where finding it later makes the גט invalid.

phrases.english: and there, it is in a place where caravans are not common.
phrases.notes: There means the ברייתא, which returns the גט even after a long time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: כָּאן בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהַשְּׁיָירוֹת מְצוּיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... וכאן): each source refers to a different kind of place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about whether a גט found after a long time can be used.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a place where caravans are common and the ברייתא is about a place where they are rare, so the two sources do not disagree.

steps.title: First version: רבי זירא agrees with רבה
steps.stepSummary: One version says רבי זירא forbids returning the גט only when it is known that two people with the same names live there. That is the same as רבה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the rule that we do not return it applies only when it is known that there are two people with the same names. This is the same as רבה's ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first version of how far רבי זירא's ruling goes. In this version, a place where caravans are common is not enough by itself to stop us from returning the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said we do not return the גט in a place where caravans are common. This version adds a condition: we hold back only if it is also known that two people in town have the same names. With that condition, רבי זירא ends up saying exactly what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; this brings in another version of a teaching
It was established or known (here, that two people have the same names)
And this is the same as

phrases.english: There are those who say:
And that is only where it was established that we should not return it,
phrases.notes: He means it is known that two couples in town have the same names. In that case רבי זירא says not to return the גט.

phrases.english: And this is the same as רבה's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: וְהוּא שֶׁהוּחְזְקוּ דְּלָא נַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how broad רבי זירא's answer in step 10 is and links it to רבה's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in a place where caravans are common, we hold back the גט only if two people with the same names are known. This matches רבה.

steps.title: Second version: רבי זירא disagrees with רבה
steps.stepSummary: Another version says that in a place where caravans are common, רבי זירא does not return the גט even if two people with the same names are not known. This disagrees with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even if it was not established that there are two people with the same names, we do not return it. This disagrees with רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי זירא's ruling. In this version, common caravans alone are enough to stop us from returning the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we do not need to know about two people with the same names. The very fact that travelers often pass through is enough to hold the גט back. רבה returns the גט unless two people with the same names are known, so the two אמוראים disagree.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Even if it was not established
phrases.notes: In a place where caravans are common, even if nobody knows of two people with the same names.

phrases.english: we should not return it,
and this disagrees with רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הוּחְזְקוּ לָא נַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the ruling in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place where caravans are common, we do not return the גט even without known people of the same names. This disagrees with רבה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי זירא. In one, he needs two people with the same names to be known before holding back the גט, just like רבה. In the other, common caravans alone are enough, so he disagrees with רבה.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי זירא use רבה's approach?
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense that רבה built his question on the משנה, because a משנה is a stronger source to ask from. But why did רבי זירא not ask from the משנה the way רבה did?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבה did not explain it like רבי זירא, because to him a משנה is a stronger source for raising a difficulty. But רבי זירא, what is his reason for not explaining it like רבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two אמוראים' methods. It understands רבה's choice of source and asks why רבי זירא chose differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה raised his contradiction from the משנה, while רבי זירא raised his from a ברייתא. Choosing the משנה makes sense, because a משנה is a stronger, more exact source. So why would רבי זירא leave the משנה and use a weaker ברייתא instead?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that; this sets up an 'X is fine, but Y?' question

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּה לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: Granted, רבה does not say it like רבי זירא,
phrases.notes: He means רבה did not build his question on the ברייתא the way רבי זירא did.

phrases.english: since to him the משנה is stronger to raise a difficulty from.
But רבי זירא,
what is the reason he does not say it like רבה?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּה לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what the rulings say to why each אמורא chose his source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי זירא raised his contradiction from a ברייתא and not from the stronger משנה that רבה used

steps.title: The משנה does not clearly say 'even after a long time'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא could say that the משנה only says 'if he says give it, we give it.' It never says 'even after a long time.' It could mean only when the document was found right away, so he asked from the ברייתא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: Does the משנה teach 'if he said give it, we give it, even after a long time'? Perhaps it means 'if he said give it, we give it,' but really, as we hold, only when it was found right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי זירא. The משנה is not clear enough to ask from, so he used the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read 'even after a long time' into the משנה, but that is only a guess from its wording. רבי זירא says the משנה may be talking only about a document found right away, which matches the rule we already hold. If so, there is no contradiction from the משנה, and only the ברייתא gives a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you; this answers for someone who is not present

phrases.english: He could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: מִי קָא תָנֵי: הָא אָמַר ״תְּנוּ״ – נוֹתְנִין
phrases.english: Does it teach: if he said 'Give it,' we give it,
and even after a long time?
Perhaps it means: if he said 'Give it,' we give it,
but really, as we hold, only right away.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה from step 8: a lost גט may be used only if it was found right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ, מִי קָא תָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה never says 'even after a long time.' It may mean only right away, so it gives no clear contradiction. The ברייתא is clearer, so רבי זירא asked from it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי זירא says the ברייתא is stronger than the משנה. He agrees a משנה is stronger. He just reads this משנה as not saying 'even after a long time' at all.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement between רבי זירא and רבה?
steps.stepSummary: According to the version where רבי זירא disagrees with רבה, the גמרא asks what their disagreement is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says that, for רבי זירא, in a place where caravans are common we do not return it even if it was not established that there are two people named יוסף בן שמעון, and so he disagrees with רבה: what are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second version from step 12 and asks for the reason behind the disagreement. This sets up the next step, where the answer will come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, רבי זירא holds back the גט just because caravans are common. רבה returns it unless two people with the same names are known. The גמרא wants to know what basic idea each one holds that leads to these different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: According to the one who says that for רבי זירא,
in a place where caravans are common,
phrases.notes: The words 'we do not return it' are left out here, but they are assumed.

phrases.english: and even if it was not established
that there are two people named Yosef ben Shimon,
and so he disagrees with רבה,
about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְרַבִּי זֵירָא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהַשְּׁיָירוֹת מְצוּיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about sources and goes back to the second version from step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basic reason behind the disagreement between רבי זירא and רבה, according to the version where they disagree

steps.title: רבה's reasoning from the court-documents משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה learns from the משנה that court documents found in court are returned, even though a court is like a place where caravans are common, unless two people with the same names are known to be there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה holds that since the משנה teaches 'any court document should be returned,' it must be talking about a document found in the court. A court is like a place where caravans are common. So he says: only if it is known that two people share the name should it not be returned; if that is not known, it should be returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from step 15. It shows that רבה's opinion comes from how he reads a משנה about court documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people from many places pass through a court, so a court is like a place where caravans are common. Yet the משנה says to return court documents anyway. רבה concludes that a busy place by itself is not a reason to hold back a found document. We only hold it back when it is known that two people have the same names.

keyTerms.meaning: Court documents, papers made or approved by a court
Caravans, groups of travelers passing through
It is established, known for sure (here: that two people share the name)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two משניות. The one quoted here, about court documents, is a different משנה from the one in מסכת גיטין about a messenger who lost a גט (step 8). Neither משנה mentions caravans. The caravans idea comes from the אמוראים in the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rabba holds
that since it teaches: Any court document
phrases.notes: This is a משנה a little later in our פרק, on 20a.

phrases.english: he should return it,
we are dealing with one that was found in court,
and a court is like a place where caravans are common,
and only where it is established, he should not return it,
phrases.notes: Established means it is known that two people with these same names live there.

phrases.english: where it is not established, he should return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה סָבַר דְּקָתָנֵי כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין הֲרֵי זֶה יַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by showing רבה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the disagreement between רבה and רבי זירא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה reads the משנה of court documents as talking about documents found inside the court, which is like a caravan place, and they are still returned unless two people with the same names are known.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the משנה never says the documents were found in court
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects רבה's reading. The משנה does not say 'found in court,' so it can be about documents found outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא would tell you: Does the משנה say 'any court document that was found in court'? It only says 'any court document should be returned.' Really, it is talking about one found outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on רבה's proof. He says the משנה can be read in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's proof only works if the documents were found inside the court, the busy caravan-like place. רבי זירא points out that the words 'found in court' are not in the משנה. If the documents were found outside, the משנה tells us nothing about busy places, so רבי זירא can still hold that in a caravan place we do not return the document even when no two people with the same names are known.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach? (a way of saying: the text does not say that)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole fight between רבה and רבי זירא comes down to one question: was the court document in that משנה found inside the court or outside it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira would say to you:
Does it teach, 'Any court documents
that were found in court'?
It teaches, 'Any court document, he should return,'
and really it is where it was found outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר לָךְ: מִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's reading of the משנה from step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's proof from the court-documents משנה, but does not disprove רבה's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה never says the documents were found in court. They may have been found outside.

steps.title: רבי יִרְמְיָה: the witnesses signed only one גט for this name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יִרְמְיָה answers the contradiction a new way: the found גט is returned when the witnesses say they only ever signed one גט for יוסף בן שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is a case where the witnesses say, 'We never signed on any גט of יוסף בן שמעון except one.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different way to fix the contradiction between our משנה, which returns a found גט, and the משנה in מסכת גיטין, which does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רבי זירא focused on the place where the גט was found. רבי יִרמְיָה focuses on the witnesses instead. If they say they signed only one גט with these names, the found גט must be that one. So there is no worry that it belongs to some other couple.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, it is a case where

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the solution from where the גט was found to proof from the witnesses about who it belongs to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said,
for example, where the witnesses say:
We never signed except

phrases.aramaic: עַל גֵּט אֶחָד שֶׁל יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: on one גט of Yosef ben Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר, כְּגוֹן דְּקָא אָמְרִי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה and רבי זירא discussion and offers a new answer to the original contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: our משנה is about a case where the witnesses confirm there was only one such גט.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seems to return a found גט in any case, which clashes with the משנה in מסכת גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is returned only when the witnesses testify they signed only one גט for this name.

steps.title: If so, why would the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יִרְמְיָה: if the witnesses already prove whose גט it is, obviously it gets returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יִרְמְיָה's answer. In his case the ruling seems too obvious to need a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach something obvious. If the witnesses say there was only one such גט, it clearly belongs to this man. So why would the משנה bother telling us to return it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יִרְמְיָה's answer from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יִרְמְיָה's explanation of our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the witnesses prove the גט is his, the ruling is obvious, and a משנה would not need to teach it.

steps.title: We might have worried that the names and witnesses just happened to match
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed because we might have worried that another couple and other witnesses had exactly the same names. The משנה teaches that this is not a worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry that maybe it just happened that the names matched other names and the witnesses matched other witnesses. So the משנה teaches us that we do not worry about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יִרְמְיָה by showing that the ruling is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe a different couple with the same names had a גט signed by different witnesses who also had the same names as these witnesses. If so, these witnesses could truthfully say they signed only one. The משנה teaches that such a double coincidence is too unlikely to worry about, so the גט is returned.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a way of showing why a ruling is needed)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יִרְמְיָה, a found גט is returned when the witnesses confirm they signed only one such גט. We do not worry about a double coincidence of matching names and matching witnesses.

phrases.english: You might have said, let us worry
perhaps it happened that a name was like a name,
and witnesses were like witnesses,
so it teaches us that we do not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא אִתְרְמִי שְׁמָא כִּשְׁמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the ruling is not obvious, because of a possible worry that it removes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have worried that the names of the couple and the witnesses matched by chance.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about such a coincidence, so the גט is returned.

steps.title: A found גט is returned when the owner names an exact hole
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the found גט is returned when the person claiming it says there is a hole next to a specific letter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: we return it in a case where he says, 'It has a hole next to such-and-such a letter.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new way to answer the contradiction about returning a found גט. It is returned when the claimant describes a very exact mark on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier answers relied on the witnesses or on the names. רב אשי's answer relies on a סימן, an identifying mark, instead. The mark he gives as an example is very exact: a hole beside one particular letter.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers a new answer here
For example, in a case where

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
For example, where he says:
phrases.notes: "He" is the person who says he lost the גט and wants it back.

phrases.english: There is a hole in it
next to such-and-such a letter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, כְּגוֹן דְּקָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction instead of רבי ירמיה's answer about the witnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the source that returns the גט is talking about a claimant who gives an exact סימן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to clash: one returns a found גט, while the משנה in מסכת גיטין says a גט not found right away is invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is returned when the claimant identifies it with a precise mark, like a hole beside a named letter.

steps.title: Only a hole by a named letter counts, not just any hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב אשי means specifically a hole next to a named letter. Simply saying 'it has a hole' is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And specifically next to such-and-such a letter. But a plain hole, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the limits of רב אשי's answer clearer. The exact location of the hole matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole somewhere in a document is a weak, general mark that could fit many papers. Naming the letter it sits next to makes it a very exact mark. רב אשי accepts only the exact kind for a גט.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי accepts any hole as a סימן. Only a hole whose exact place is described counts here.

phrases.english: And specifically next to such-and-such a letter,
but just a hole – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא בְּצַד אוֹת פְּלוֹנִית, אֲבָל נֶקֶב בְּעָלְמָא – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out exactly what kind of mark רב אשי requires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an exact סימן (a hole beside a named letter) gets a found גט returned. A general mark like 'a hole' does not.

steps.title: Why רב אשי wants such an exact mark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אשי is unsure whether סימנים are trusted by Torah law or only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי is unsure whether סימנים are from the Torah or from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רב אשי's strict requirement from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סימנים only work מדרבנן, they might not be strong enough for something serious like a גט. Because רב אשי is unsure, he relies only on a mark so exact that it surely works even by Torah law. That explains why a plain hole is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks used to claim a lost item
From the Torah, by Torah law
From the Rabbis, by rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: a found גט is returned only with a very exact סימן, because he is unsure if ordinary סימנים are trusted מדאורייתא or only מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether סימנים work by Torah law or rabbinic law is a big question that comes up in many places. It decides when we can rely on them for serious matters like a גט.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi is unsure about identifying marks
whether they are from the Torah or from the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ סִימָנִים אִי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אִי דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the limit stated in the last step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because רב אשי is unsure about the strength of סימנים, he relies only on a precise סימן for a גט.

steps.title: Opening a story about רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story about רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening words of a new story. The גמרא is setting up the next part, which continues after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name רבה בר בר חנה appears here. What happened to him will be told in the next lines, so we cannot explain it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא; the main person of the story that is starting

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב אשי's answer to a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. The story continues after this section.
